summary: A pop-up form for logging or editing a hackathon, with an AI box that can fill the fields from a typed description.
purpose: Lets the user add or change hackathon details quickly, including by describing the event in plain words.
why: Likely reason: AI fill saves typing. Reason for showing the form in a pop-up is not stated in the code.
how: 1. Set each field from the existing hackathon, or blank for a new one. 2. When the user asks the AI to fill the form, send the text to the AI service and copy its reply into the fields. 3. Show a note asking the user to check the fields. 4. On save, clean up the text, split the lists, then update or add the record and close the window.
inputs: Typed field values, an optional existing hackathon, and the typed text for AI fill.
outputs: A new or updated hackathon saved to the store, and the window closes.
risks: Typed text is sent to an outside AI service. A failed AI call only writes to the console, so the user sees no message. A partial AI reply can erase what the user typed. A blank title is ignored silently.
debug: If AI fill does nothing, open the browser console and look for the logged parse error, then check the AI provider setup. If saved team or tech entries look wrong, check how the comma split is done. If the window will not open, check the open setting passed in by the parent screen. Note that sections 5 to 7 were not provided, so this review is partial.
